e0f897808a5cc46ec01fe4f7aaebf0f03e8a6cd8: These provisions collectively regulate the compliance framework for specific goods and the operational definitions governing principal-agent relationships under the GST regime. Section 148A serves as the central provision, as it mandates a unique identification marking system for notified goods and persons, while Section 122B establishes the punitive consequences for failing to adhere to these specific marking requirements. Other provisions, such as those defining agents and principal supplies, provide the necessary legal context to determine liability and scope when these identification and supply obligations are executed.
65821df21773521f23de5cb184a7cfd229ecaa19: These provisions collectively regulate the foundational framework for the levy, collection, and administrative relief of Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) in India. Section 9 of the CGST Act serves as the central provision, establishing the primary legal authority and scope for taxing intra-State supplies. The remaining notifications and circulars act as supplementary instruments that define specific operational timelines, clarify the taxability of unique supply categories, and provide the government with discretionary powers under Section 11A to waive tax liabilities arising from prevalent industry practices.
deaec2d5d12bac8c8050fdc60bc1addfe8b8f844: These provisions collectively regulate the scope of taxable supply and the subsequent determination, apportionment, and reversal of Input Tax Credit (ITC). Section 17 of the CGST Act serves as the central provision, establishing the fundamental principles for credit eligibility, blocked credits, and the necessity of apportionment for non-business or exempt activities. Schedules II and III define the boundaries of what constitutes a supply, while the associated Rules (38-44) and Circulars provide the technical mechanisms and formulas required to calculate, distribute, and reverse ITC in alignment with the core mandates of Section 17.
9f4e976fd66cad3c21d471f619e75d8240040aaf: These provisions collectively regulate the tax liability and compliance framework for services supplied under the Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) and the subsequent distribution of input tax credit. Section 13 of the CGST Act serves as the central provision, establishing the critical "time of supply" that dictates when tax liability arises for these transactions. The various entries in Notifications 10/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate) and 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate) act as the operational triggers, identifying specific service categories and recipients subject to RCM, while Section 20 provides the mechanism for Input Service Distributors to manage and distribute the resulting tax credits across distinct business entities.
90cbc00dbf15fb11d36f605afe0c1a2ada82dbf1: These provisions collectively regulate the framework for job work operations, the movement of goods without immediate tax invoices, and the administrative oversight required for uniform compliance. Section 143 serves as the central provision, establishing the core legal mechanism for sending goods to job workers without tax liability. Sections 19, 45, and 55 act as supporting operational pillars that define Input Tax Credit eligibility and the documentation requirements for these movements, while Sections 167, 168, and the associated circulars provide the necessary administrative authority and interpretive guidance to ensure consistent enforcement across the GST regime.
e81286d7d5748746dec1b9f86af80e4544466883: Sections 16, 41, 155 of the CGST Act and Rule 37A collectively regulate the eligibility, claiming process, and mandatory reversal conditions for Input Tax Credit (ITC). Section 16 serves as the central provision, establishing the fundamental requirements for claiming credit, while Section 41 and Rule 37A act as procedural mechanisms that enforce compliance by mandating reversals if the supplier fails to pay the underlying tax. Section 155 reinforces this framework by placing the legal burden of proof on the taxpayer to substantiate their eligibility for these claims. (Note: The provided circular regarding rental service rates is unrelated to the ITC compliance framework established by these specific sections.)
2bef55b71cb5121b66ee80aed42c2fe38c35dd28: Sections 90, 91, 93, and 94 of the CGST Act, 2017, collectively regulate the continuity and enforcement of tax liabilities when a business entity undergoes structural changes, dissolution, or representation by a fiduciary. Section 93 serves as the central provision, establishing the overarching framework for successor liability upon the death, partition, or termination of an entity. Sections 90, 91, and 94 function as specific extensions of this principle, detailing how liability is apportioned among partners, guardians, and members during ongoing operations, reconstitution, or the cessation of business activities. Together, these provisions ensure that tax obligations remain enforceable against the responsible parties regardless of changes in the entity's legal status.
9a534bb32a5471d79684621468be8c4b1d7eafaf: These provisions collectively regulate the framework for legal representation and the evidentiary procedures governing GST inquiries. Section 70 serves as the central provision, establishing the authority to summon individuals for evidence and defining such inquiries as judicial proceedings. Sections 116, 48, and their associated rules define the eligibility and conduct of authorized representatives and GST practitioners who facilitate these appearances, while Section 136 ensures the admissibility of evidence gathered during these formal proceedings.
c8ecae757908793992b810294611bcc9904be560: These provisions collectively regulate the comprehensive dispute resolution and appellate framework under the GST regime, spanning from initial administrative appeals to final adjudication by the Supreme Court. Section 107 serves as the central pillar, establishing the primary procedure for filing appeals against departmental orders, while the subsequent sections and rules define the hierarchy of the Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT), the scope of judicial review by High Courts, and the specific procedural requirements for filing, withdrawal, and compliance. Together, these linked provisions ensure a structured, multi-tiered mechanism for taxpayers to challenge assessments and for the government to exercise revisional oversight.
5fe346c193071f4a36c54835abc68373f5a49336: These provisions collectively regulate the compliance and enforcement framework for high-risk manufacturing sectors requiring special oversight. Section 148 serves as the central provision, granting the government the authority to mandate specific registration procedures for certain classes of goods. Section 122A acts as the enforcement mechanism by imposing penalties for failing to register machines under those special procedures, while Section 71 provides the operational power for officers to enter premises and verify that these registration and compliance requirements are being met.
e9d7b3c859b261d8a4d2c6a93f58bc00b521a39b: These provisions collectively regulate the scope and taxability of "supply" under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. Section 7 of the Act serves as the central provision, establishing the fundamental definition of supply as an activity performed for consideration in the course of business. The various circulars and notifications relate to this core provision by clarifying whether specific transactions—such as director remuneration, liquidated damages, or charitable donations—constitute a taxable supply or fall outside the tax net due to the absence of a clear contractual exchange or commercial intent.
6d31f8622551be1eb1e825cebbfd7e95a523df64: These provisions collectively regulate the collection, management, and confidentiality of information under the GST framework. Section 150 serves as the central pillar, establishing the mandatory obligation for various entities to file information returns, while Sections 151 and 153 provide the administrative authority to gather and analyze this data. Sections 123 and 124 enforce compliance through penalties, whereas Sections 152, 158, and 158A act as critical safeguards to protect taxpayer privacy and restrict the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information. Finally, Sections 111, 128, and 133 provide the necessary oversight, including judicial powers, penalty waivers, and criminal sanctions for the misuse of official data.
605f8a69e2bca881d829d3e688272e7dff42a4cb: These provisions collectively regulate the anti-profiteering framework under the GST regime, ensuring that businesses pass on the benefits of tax rate reductions or input tax credits to consumers. Section 171 of the CGST Act serves as the central legislative mandate, establishing the legal obligation for price reductions and the government's authority to enforce them. The associated CGST Rules, specifically Rules 123 through 136, function as the procedural machinery that operationalizes this mandate by defining the investigative hierarchy, the methodology for assessment, and the remedial powers of the authorities. Finally, Section 57 acts as a supporting provision by providing a destination for recovered funds, such as penalties or unclaimed benefits, to be credited to the Consumer Welfare Fund.
9b161654651373cd0a46dcce7b268f1aeede5c7f: Sections 173 and 174 of the CGST Act, 2017, jointly regulate the transition from the legacy indirect tax regime to the GST framework by formally repealing previous service tax and excise laws. Section 174 serves as the central provision, as it establishes the legal mechanism for repealing these enactments while simultaneously preserving ongoing rights, liabilities, and investigations to ensure continuity. Section 173 acts as a specific corollary to this transition, explicitly omitting the Finance Act, 1994, to clear the legislative path for the new tax structure.
2696d34bfe72625ff8bd33a85791ad528acfe0c2: These provisions collectively regulate the taxation and compliance framework for cross-border supplies of Online Information and Database Access or Retrieval (OIDAR) services and online money gaming. Section 14 and Section 14A of the IGST Act serve as the central pillars, establishing the legal liability for overseas suppliers to pay integrated tax and obtain simplified registration. Rules 14 and 64 of the CGST Rules operationalize these sections by mandating specific electronic application and filing procedures for these foreign entities. Finally, the cited notifications provide the necessary regulatory context by defining the scope of reverse charge mechanisms and specific exemptions applicable to these cross-border transactions.
99ccf79665a0cc86c92653acd4b8e86d678254af: These provisions collectively regulate the lifecycle of GST registration, encompassing the procedural requirements for obtaining, maintaining, and cancelling a registration. Section 29 of the CGST Act serves as the central provision, establishing the legal authority for the cancellation of registration, while the associated rules and sections provide the necessary framework for suspension, revocation, and the procedural validity of these administrative actions. Specifically, Sections 30, 160, 161, and 169, alongside Rules 10A through 23, function as supporting mechanisms that define the operational steps for compliance, the correction of errors, and the legal service of notices during the registration management process.
a5c8f0b700645aadf2df3432320f276b692a4f69: This group of provisions collectively regulates the comprehensive framework for claiming, processing, and sanctioning Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds. Section 54 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, serves as the central provision, establishing the fundamental legal authority and procedural requirements for refund claims. The remaining sections and rules act as supporting mechanisms, detailing specific scenarios such as deemed exports (Section 147), interest on delayed payments (Section 56), and the operational procedures for filing, scrutiny, and disbursement (Rules 89–96).
6b3c60885210084197b3fb9f5dd7772413d46e59: These provisions collectively regulate the valuation of taxable supplies under the GST framework to ensure accurate tax assessment. Section 15 of the CGST Act serves as the central provision, establishing the transaction value as the primary basis for valuation when consideration is paid between unrelated parties. The remaining rules and schedules act as supplementary mechanisms, providing specific methodologies for determining value when transactions involve non-monetary consideration, related parties, agents, or unique sectors like online gaming and insurance.
943b3f7426d48128775aa0f57962f15472a04d5c: Sections 12 and 14 of the CGST Act, 2017, jointly regulate the determination of the time of supply for goods and services to establish tax liability. Section 12 serves as the central provision by defining the standard rules for the time of supply, while Section 14 acts as a specific override that dictates how to calculate the time of supply during periods of tax rate changes. Other related provisions, such as Rule 34 and Notification 66/2017, rely on these sections to determine the applicable exchange rates for valuation and the specific timing for tax payments by registered persons.
8a37146b7db4ca9d06491c0781a538fa027bf1d4: These provisions collectively establish the administrative and interpretive framework required to enforce the Goods and Services Tax regime. Section 3 of the CGST Act serves as the central provision by legally empowering the officers responsible for administering the law. The cited notifications relate to this central authority by providing the specific definitions and classifications necessary for these officers to consistently apply tax rates and interpret legal terms across various sectors.
dae09da41acc6ebeefeb70d1a341c6b5994c13f9: These provisions collectively regulate the documentation, issuance, and evidentiary requirements for taxable transactions under the GST framework. Section 31 of the CGST Act serves as the central pillar, mandating the issuance of invoices, vouchers, and credit/debit notes for various supply scenarios. The associated rules and circulars act as operational extensions, prescribing the specific mandatory particulars, timelines, and procedural adjustments necessary to ensure compliance and facilitate the valid claim of input tax credit.
0aefd2fbace29472946ca39142ffb795918c4946: These provisions collectively regulate the end-to-end compliance framework for GST reporting, encompassing the declaration of outward supplies, the filing of periodic and annual returns, and the assessment of tax liabilities. The remaining sections and rules function as supporting mechanisms by prescribing the specific procedures for reporting outward supplies (Section 37), facilitating input tax credit visibility (Section 38), enforcing filing deadlines through notices and penalties (Sections 46 and 47), and detailing specialized reporting requirements for entities like e-commerce operators (Section 52).
425db0c7125267357e17879fb9e83d0d69b03c83: These provisions collectively regulate the electronic management of tax liabilities, the maintenance of cash and credit ledgers, and the cross-utilization of input tax credits across different tax jurisdictions. The remaining sections and rules function as supporting mechanisms that define the specific order of credit utilization, mandate the maintenance of detailed registers, and govern the inter-governmental financial transfers required to balance tax accounts when credits are applied across central, state, and integrated tax heads.
2993442d082fddd64fdc629c5483799a2bed5add: This collection of provisions jointly regulates the assessment, audit, and adjudication framework for tax compliance and enforcement under the GST regime. Sections 73, 74, and 74A serve as the central pillars, establishing the core procedures for determining tax liabilities, interest, and penalties arising from non-payment or erroneous refunds. The remaining provisions relate to these sections by defining the investigative triggers (such as scrutiny, audit, and assessment), prescribing specific penalties and enforcement measures (like confiscation and property attachment), and detailing the procedural rules for electronic communication and recovery.
b70270a7b51986df12b87a21ae6909490af34600: These provisions collectively regulate the Advance Ruling mechanism under the GST framework, which allows taxpayers to seek clarity on tax liabilities and classifications. 63a1daa37386af3268e2c2094147ceb8a478e61f: These provisions collectively regulate the documentation, maintenance, and verification of records required for tax compliance and the movement of goods under the GST regime. The remaining rules and circulars act as operational extensions, detailing the specific requirements for invoice generation, the mandatory e-way bill system for transit, and the procedural standards for record retention and audit.
a33c42368bd52b5042b4722f5aa7f8c0b080254f: These provisions collectively regulate the legal framework for GST enforcement, specifically governing the delegation of rule-making powers and the procedural execution of search and seizure operations. Section 67 serves as the central provision, establishing the substantive authority for tax officers to conduct inspections and seize assets in cases of suspected evasion. 0900be1257f79baca720219e1b19f929d8831bbf: These provisions collectively regulate the recovery of unpaid tax, interest, and penalties under the GST framework. Section 79 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, serves as the central provision, establishing the legal authority for the proper officer to initiate recovery through various methods such as property attachment, sale of goods, and third-party notices. The remaining sections and rules act as procedural extensions, detailing the specific mechanisms for enforcement, defining the liability of directors and liquidators, and outlining the administrative assistance required to execute these recovery orders.
bfaaea63951ad09daee5dddb3d3334262d59ae6b: These provisions collectively regulate the framework and application of tax exemptions for inter-State services under the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) regime. 40daa764d3b6eafc57dc913d2da3ea99430c0c4e: Sections 7 and 8 of the IGST Act serve as the central provisions, establishing the fundamental framework for classifying supplies as either inter-State or intra-State based on the relationship between the supplier's location and the place of supply. c41c664b4a1fe0cc2011e8f58dce108ef4e9fa4c: These provisions collectively regulate the determination of the place of supply for services that span multiple States or Union Territories, particularly when contractual values are not clearly segregated. Sections 12 and 13 of the IGST Act serve as the central framework, establishing the primary rules for domestic and cross-border supply, respectively. The IGST Rules (Rules 3 through 9) and Circular 103/22/2019-GST act as supplementary mechanisms that provide specific methodologies for apportioning value across jurisdictions when the central rules cannot be applied due to a lack of distinct contractual allocation.
48bb65bdaa2ae49dd2ed197b4f2e102b50bb80d3: These provisions collectively establish the regulatory framework for the administration and procedural application of the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST). Section 20 of the IGST Act serves as the central provision, as it mandates the adoption of CGST procedures for IGST purposes, while Rule 2 of the IGST Rules operationalizes this by aligning the application of CGST rules to integrated tax. Together, these sections ensure a cohesive administrative structure by bridging IGST requirements with the established CGST procedural regime.
4ca9f2885f9e6c4bba72ba3f70afb0dd2a84a8a2: These provisions collectively regulate the administrative framework, transitional mechanisms, and legal application of the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax (UTGST) Act. Sections 3, 5, 6, and 11 establish the hierarchy and powers of tax officers, while Section 21 ensures the seamless integration of CGST provisions into the UTGST framework. Finally, Sections 8 and 18 provide the specific operational rules for tax exemptions and the transition of input tax credits, respectively.
976676f2b997bf3a2d3448e6b1b2f6c775de0161: These provisions collectively regulate the scope of GST exemptions for essential public services, specifically focusing on healthcare and governmental functions. 925eff9207e2e4a98dc6643c8c8369cb0cd772c3: These provisions collectively regulate the scope of GST exemptions for various essential services, such as education, transportation, and public utilities. baa3e2d47775c4d3e934ed491a502da6c25fd456: These provisions collectively regulate the scope and application of GST exemptions for various services under Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate). 24f1926a859111d3492634d39df1e2a877bf198c: These provisions collectively regulate the GST exemption framework for various insurance and reinsurance services provided under government-backed welfare schemes. f8e6ddade37944a44dc881229ebf6fa509200dfd: These provisions collectively regulate the taxability of services provided by business facilitators and correspondents within the banking sector. Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Entry 39, serves as the central provision by granting specific exemptions for these services when provided to rural bank branches. Notifications No. 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Entries 12 and 13, act as the operational framework by mandating that the banking company or business correspondent must pay the tax under the reverse charge mechanism for any services not covered by the aforementioned exemption.
9e87dee18318eb00424d89684824fdc749c8f335: These provisions collectively regulate the taxability and valuation of development rights, floor space index (FSI), and long-term land leases used in real estate construction. Together, they ensure that the transfer of land-related rights is taxed proportionally based on the status of apartment bookings.
abe1ce63282d8f24f6f4f9f045c035aa592bf137: These provisions collectively regulate the exemption of agricultural and essential services from GST to reduce the tax burden on the primary sector. 86ec9e9e86d91b7c3dc371ff2ebabfcb9d5f7432: Circular No. 82/01/2019-GST serves as the central regulatory framework for determining the GST liability of services provided by Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs). 443e6d91c56940ca4b3012e00cfb75e27026c5dc: These provisions collectively regulate the tax liability mechanism for specific services, shifting the responsibility from the service provider to the recipient under the Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM). 237c43a05fde06f4187bcd476007bf02bd837326: These provisions collectively regulate the Composition Levy scheme, which allows eligible small taxpayers to pay GST at a simplified, fixed rate based on their turnover. Section 10 of the CGST Act serves as the central provision, establishing the legal framework, eligibility criteria, and turnover thresholds for the scheme. c19670866a958d8c1758f547f81af0fe94a15478: These linked provisions collectively regulate the taxability and valuation of land-related inputs, such as Transferable Development Rights (TDR), Floor Space Index (FSI), and long-term lease premiums, used by promoters for real estate construction. a88e3f1c7e500f5362d9fe9b779b7806e87533da: These provisions collectively regulate the taxability of business facilitator and business correspondent services provided to banking and insurance sectors under the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) framework. 021f2ccec015094ea701d30c49743e70c763fa66: These provisions collectively regulate the scope and application of Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) on various economic activities.
